## Purpose

Standalone walkthrough of the generic GLMM model factory (`3_analysis/R/functions_statistics.R`) applied to the `yield_dry` and `quality_n` outcomes, plus the 2 existing preliminary yield figures (unchanged) and a new estimated-marginal-means plot per outcome. Calls `2_preprocessing/R/functions_yield_quality.R` and `3_analysis/R/functions_yield_analysis.R` directly.

It also reproduces the manuscript's **Figure 1** (`4_outputs/main_figures/Fig01_crop_productivity.{pdf,png}`) from scratch (Step 6) -- running this document end to end regenerates that figure exactly as `targets::tar_make(c("fig01_result", "fig01_file", "fig01_caption_file"))` does, since both call the same `assemble_fig01()` / `save_manuscript_figure()` functions. Re-run Step 6 alone (or the whole document) any time the underlying data, model, or plotting code changes.

```{r setup}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(kableExtra)
library(gt)
library(glmmTMB)
library(DHARMa)
library(car)
library(emmeans)
library(patchwork)

source(here("2_preprocessing", "R", "functions_yield_quality.R"))
source(here("3_analysis", "R", "functions_yield_analysis.R"))
source(here("3_analysis", "R", "functions_statistics.R"))
source(here("3_analysis", "R", "functions_manuscript_figures.R"))
source(here("3_analysis", "R", "fig01_crop_productivity.R"))
source(here("3_analysis", "R", "utils.R"))
source(here("3_analysis", "R", "plot_theme.R"))
```

## Step 1: Build the analysis-ready dataset

```{r build-data}
#| message: false
study2_yield_analysis_ready <- build_study2_yield_dataset(
  xlsx_2023 = here("1_input_data", "crop_yield_quality", "2023", "HYPERFARM_YIELD_DATA_2023_v2.xlsx"),
  xlsx_2024 = here("1_input_data", "crop_yield_quality", "2024", "HYPERFARM_VALUE4FARM_YIELD_DATA_2024_v3.xlsx"),
  xlsx_2025 = here("1_input_data", "crop_yield_quality", "2025", "VALUE4FARM_YIELD_DATA_2025.xlsx")
)
```

## Step 2: Preliminary figures (existing, unchanged)

```{r fig-yield-treatment}

plot_yield_by_treatment(study2_yield_analysis_ready)
```

```{r fig-yield-location}
#| fig-width: 9
```

## Step 3: Fit, diagnose, and test the yield model

`fit_yield_dry_model()`: `DRY_WEIGHT_TON_HA ~ GLOBAL_SUB_STRIP_LOCATION + FERTILISATION + RESIDUE + CROP_PRODUCT + YEAR + FERTILISATION:RESIDUE`, `dispformula = ~ ROW + COLUMN`, Gamma(link = "log").

```{r fit-yield}
yield_fit <- fit_yield_dry_model(study2_yield_analysis_ready)
summary(yield_fit)
```

```{r diagnose-yield}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
yield_diag <- diagnose_glmm(yield_fit)
plot(yield_diag$sim)
```

```{r anova-yield}
anova_glmm(yield_fit)
```

## Step 4: Estimated marginal means (new figure)

```{r emm-yield}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
yield_emm <- emm_yield_dry_model(yield_fit)
plot_emmeans_effect(
  as.data.frame(yield_emm$emmeans),
  x_var = "RESIDUE", colour_var = "FERTILISATION",
  colour_values = fertilisation_colors, y_lab = "Dry-matter yield (t/ha)"
)
```

## Step 5: Quality (total N%) model

Same structure, without `YEAR` (quality data currently exist only for the 2024 season -- see `fit_quality_model()`'s docstring). No preliminary figures exist for this outcome, so the emmeans plot below is its only figure.

```{r fit-quality}
quality_fit <- fit_quality_model(study2_yield_analysis_ready)
anova_glmm(quality_fit)
```

```{r emm-quality}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
quality_emm <- emm_quality_model(quality_fit)
plot_emmeans_effect(
  as.data.frame(quality_emm$emmeans),
  x_var = "RESIDUE", colour_var = "FERTILISATION",
  colour_values = fertilisation_colors, y_lab = "Total N (%)"
)
```

## Step 6: Manuscript Figure 1 -- crop productivity, quality & management response under VAPV

This is the manuscript-ready figure (`3_analysis/R/fig01_crop_productivity.R`), distinct from Steps 3-5 above. It fits 5 dedicated candidate models (`fit_yield_substrip_model`, `fit_yield_pooled_model`, `fit_quality_substrip_model`, `fit_quality_pooled_model`, `fit_yield_management_model`; see `functions_statistics.R`) and renders a 6-panel composite coloured by crop:

- **A/B**: yield by row position (EMMs) / overall VAPV effect on yield (% response forest)
- **C/D**: as A/B for tissue N (%)
- **E**: agronomic management effects on yield (fertiliser, residue), per crop
- **F**: VAPV x management interaction on yield (pooled across crop) -- does VAPV itself change the management response?

### Step 6a: fit the 5 candidate models and build each subfigure

`fig01_build_panels()` fits every candidate model and builds each of the 6 panels as a standalone ggplot object -- shown individually below before compositing, rather than only ever appearing pre-assembled.

```{r fig01-build-panels}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
fig01_panels <- fig01_build_panels(study2_yield_analysis_ready)
```

```{r fig01-model-summary}
tibble::tibble(
  model = c("yield_substrip", "yield_pooled", "quality_substrip", "quality_pooled", "yield_management"),
  formula = purrr::map_chr(fig01_panels$fits, ~ paste(deparse(stats::formula(.x)), collapse = " ")),
  n_obs = purrr::map_int(fig01_panels$fits, stats::nobs),
  converged = purrr::map_lgl(fig01_panels$fits, ~ isTRUE(.x$sdr$pdHess))
)
```

**Panel A -- yield by row position:**

```{r fig01-panel-a}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5
fig01_panels$panel_a
```

**Panel B -- overall VAPV effect on yield:**

```{r fig01-panel-b}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
fig01_panels$panel_b
```

**Panel C -- tissue N by row position:**

```{r fig01-panel-c}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5
fig01_panels$panel_c
```

**Panel D -- overall VAPV effect on tissue N:**

```{r fig01-panel-d}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
fig01_panels$panel_d
```

**Panel E -- agronomic management effects on yield (per crop):**

```{r fig01-panel-e}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5

```

**Panel F -- VAPV x management interaction on yield (pooled across crop):**

```{r fig01-panel-f}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
fig01_panels$panel_f
```

### Step 6b: assemble the composite

`fig01_assemble_composite()` takes the 6 already-built panels above and lays them out into the final manuscript figure (shared legend, tags, spacing) -- this is the SAME function `_targets.R`'s `fig01_result` target calls internally, so this composite is identical to the one `tar_make()` produces.

```{r fig01-composite}
#| fig-width: 8.0
#| fig-height: 9.2
fig01_composite <- fig01_assemble_composite(fig01_panels)
fig01_composite
```

Save to `4_outputs/main_figures/` -- the same call `_targets.R`'s `fig01_file`/`fig01_caption_file` targets make, so this reproduces those files exactly:

```{r fig01-save}
#| message: false
save_manuscript_figure(fig01_composite, "Fig01_crop_productivity",
                        subdir = "main_figures", width = 8.0, height = 9.2)
save_figure_caption(fig01_caption(), "Fig01_crop_productivity", subdir = "main_figures")
```

### Step 6c: omnibus statistical test table

Figures show effect sizes and 95% CIs; this table is the formal-test counterpart (Type II Wald chi-square tests). Built from the SAME 5 model objects `fig01_panels$fits` already fitted in Step 6a -- `anova_glmm()` (`car::Anova()`) is a Wald test on an already-fitted model, not a refit, so nothing here re-runs the (comparatively expensive) `glmmTMB()` calls a second time.

```{r fig01-omnibus-table}
fig01_result_for_table <- list(
  yield_substrip    = list(anova = as.data.frame(anova_glmm(fig01_panels$fits$yield_substrip))),
  yield_pooled      = list(anova = as.data.frame(anova_glmm(fig01_panels$fits$yield_pooled))),
  quality_substrip  = list(anova = as.data.frame(anova_glmm(fig01_panels$fits$quality_substrip))),
  quality_pooled    = list(anova = as.data.frame(anova_glmm(fig01_panels$fits$quality_pooled))),
  yield_management  = list(anova = as.data.frame(anova_glmm(fig01_panels$fits$yield_management)))
)
fig01_omnibus <- fig01_omnibus_table(fig01_result_for_table)
fig01_omnibus |>
  kableExtra::kbl(digits = 3, caption = "Figure 1: omnibus (Type II Wald chi-square) tests per model") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r fig01-omnibus-save}
#| message: false
save_report_table(gt::fmt_number(gt::gt(fig01_omnibus), columns = c(Df, Chisq, P), decimals = 3),
                   fig01_omnibus, "manuscript", "Fig01_omnibus_tests")
```
